name: BrowserSkill
description: Let AI agents use your real, logged-in browser without interrupting your work. CLI + extension for browser automation across any shell-capable AI agent.

# BrowserSkill

Your agent. Your browser. One connection.
Turn the browser you already use into a workspace for your AI agent.

English · 中文
Website · Demo · Features · Website debugging · Documentation · Changelog

**BrowserSkill connects your AI agent to Chrome or Microsoft Edge, using your existing logins.** Give it a task to read, click, fill, or investigate. Work stays visible in a separate **Agent Window**, and you can take over when needed. Existing tabs can be explicitly borrowed and returned when the task ends. ## See it in action
▶ Watch the demo · 81 seconds · English
 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6111d978-baa6-4a76-92c4-4f51d47ae617

Click the cover to expand the video · Download MP4
Real browser actions on a local demo workspace, recorded from main.

## Bring the agent you already use

Codex
Claude Code
Cursor
OpenClaw

CodeBuddy
WorkBuddy
Pi
Hermes Agent
Qoder, Qoder CN, and DeepSeek Harness are also supported as skill targets (`bsk install-skill --harness qoder`, `--harness qoder-cn`, and `--harness dsh`), and **[DeepSeek Harness](#deepseek-harness-plugin)** also provides a lightweight plugin (`@wxg-prc-cpg/browser-skill-dsh-plugin`) with bundled skill registration and on-demand `bsk` CLI setup. These and other agents that can run shell commands use the same **`bsk` CLI**, and MCP clients can also connect through **`bsk mcp`** ([MCP setup](docs/mcp.md)). You choose the agent and model; BrowserSkill connects it to your browser. ## What you can do | Your goal | What BrowserSkill provides | | --- | --- | | **Work where you are already signed in** | Read documents, search internal sites, and complete web workflows with the browser's existing login state. | | **Turn instructions into browser actions** | Read page text and controls, click, type, fill forms, drag items, select ranges, and manage tabs. Capture viewport or full-page screenshots; upload and download files in local mode. | | **Stay in control of the task** | Work alongside the agent with shared control, pause it while you edit, and let it reconcile your changes before continuing. Tasks remain visible in their own window; existing tabs can be explicitly borrowed. | | **Take web data with you** | Export loaded tables and lists as JSON/CSV, with column names, page/frame sources, merged-cell metadata, and explicit coverage. [Structured extraction](docs/structured-extraction.md) | | **Find the evidence behind a failure** | Connect actions to requests, response bodies, console messages, and page changes. Inspect performance, slow APIs, and suspected duplicate requests; test a hypothesis with explicit HTTP rules or request replay. [Website debugging](docs/website-debugging.md) | | **Keep a replay of the work** | Record one authorized task tab as a silent MP4, then preview, save, or delete it from the extension. [Task video recording](docs/video-recording.md) | | **Continue when the page is ready** | Wait for a requested element condition with an explicit timeout before the next step. [Element waits](docs/wait-for-element.md) | | **Reuse what you already observed** | Execute one chosen action and synchronize with `step`; explicitly save the full observation, then search or read it with `view` without another browser capture. [Steps and saved observations](crates/bsk-cli/skill/references/step-and-cache.md) | | **Use the right browser for the job** | Name browser instances, bind a task to a specific profile, or pair a server-side agent with the browser on your computer. [Browser profiles](docs/browser-profiles.md) | | **Review what happened** | Reopen browser-local debugging history, export evidence as JSON, or enable a separate operation audit to review task activity. [Operation audit](docs/operation-audit.md) | ## Quick Start For local automation, you need **an AI agent + the `bsk` CLI + the browser extension**. The CLI includes the background daemon. The skill teaches your agent how to use it. | Component | Supported environments | | --- | --- | | CLI / daemon | macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel · Linux: x64 and ARM64 · Windows: x64 | | Extension | Chrome and Microsoft Edge, based on Chromium 125 or later. Other Chromium browsers may work; compatibility is not guaranteed. | | Agent integration | A shell-capable or MCP-capable agent with the BrowserSkill skill ([MCP setup](docs/mcp.md)). | ### Let your agent set it up Send this to your agent: ```text Set up browser-skill on this machine by following https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/AGENT_INSTALL.md ``` The guide covers CLI installation, skill setup, connection checks, and a first browser task. You will still need to install the extension in the browser you want to use: **[Install for Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/hhcmgoofomhgciiibhipgmgkgnoenaoi)** · **[Install for Edge](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/browserskill/emacgiaaaiojkkpkddmmdfhmokgmnikg)**
Manual setup #### 1. Install the CLI macOS / Linux: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/install.sh | sh export PATH="${BSK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH" ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` By default, the binary is installed under `~/.local/bin`. Check it in the terminal or agent environment that will use it: ```sh bsk --version ``` If an already-running agent cannot find `bsk`, restart it to pick up the new PATH, or configure the installed binary's absolute path. #### 2. Connect the extension Install it from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/hhcmgoofomhgciiibhipgmgkgnoenaoi) or [Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/browserskill/emacgiaaaiojkkpkddmmdfhmokgmnikg), enable the connection and start using it. Local pairing is optional: an unpaired connection stays usable and shows an identity warning. To verify the connection, run `bsk daemon pair` and paste its link into **Connection settings → Pairing link**. Pairing is remembered across restarts and upgrades; a paired connection never automatically skips verification after a failure. See [local pairing](docs/local-pairing.md). #### 3. Install the skill for your agent ```sh bsk install-skill ``` Select your harness with **Space**, then press **Enter**. For non-interactive setup, choose it explicitly: ```sh bsk install-skill --harness cursor --json ``` Use `bsk install-skill --list` to see supported targets and paths. Existing installations are skipped unless you explicitly replace them with `--force`. For another harness, copy the entire [`crates/bsk-cli/skill/`](crates/bsk-cli/skill/) directory into its skills directory as `browser-skill/`, including `references/`. For MCP clients, `bsk install-skill --harness codex --mcp` also configures the local stdio server (`claude-code` and `cursor` are supported too). See the [MCP setup and workflow](docs/mcp.md). #### 4. Check the connection ```sh bsk doctor ``` Resolve any failed checks and confirm that the extension shows **Connected**. Start a new agent session and check that it can discover `browser-skill`; a successful doctor check alone does not confirm skill discovery.
### Try your first task Once connected, ask your agent: ```text Use browser-skill to open https://example.com, summarize the page, and end the browser session when finished. ``` The agent opens its own window in the background, reads the page, returns the summary, and stops its task. External links or manually created tabs that land in the task window are moved to your most recently used normal window; a user window is created if none remain. Routing happens after tab creation, so a tab may briefly appear in the task window. Page-opened tabs and human assistance or recording are preserved. Harnesses that support skill slash commands can also use `/browser-skill`. Moving any controlled tab out of its original Agent Window ends the entire browser session, preserves every page in place, and removes its control indicators. Borrowed tabs also stay where they are. Moving a tab back does not resume the task; starting again requires a user decision. Reordering tabs within the same window is unaffected. Normal session stop still returns borrowed tabs and cleans up task pages. Chrome can still activate a window when a page opens a native popup. For observed task popups, the extension restores the previous Chrome window or minimized state if you have not switched windows. Chrome's public extension APIs cannot guarantee zero transient activation or restore focus to another application.
Try the CLI directly Start a session and keep the returned `session_id`: ```sh bsk session start --json ``` Replace `` with that value in each command below. With multiple connected browsers, select one using `--browser ` when starting the session. Background creation is the default; `--no-focus` remains supported, and `--focus` explicitly brings the new window forward. Requests for human help and interactive recording still bring the relevant window forward. ```sh bsk navigate https://example.com --session bsk observe --session bsk screenshot --session --out example.png bsk session stop ``` Use `bsk --help` or `bsk --help` for comma

releases.body:
BrowserSkill Extension 0.5.0 improves the browser observations agents use, supports optional local pairing, and fixes shared-control and navigation regressions. Pair it with CLI/daemon 0.5.0.

### Added

- **Optional local pairing.** Connection settings can verify the daemon and browser identities and recover interrupted pairing. The CLI supports replacing or revoking a paired device.
- **Richer observations.** Unlabeled inputs can use nearby captions, native selects show their options, and runs of read-only table rows take fewer lines. Native select can match a unique visible option label.
- **Safer target selection.** The extension filters visually hidden instructions from observations while preserving accessible labels. It checks whether a virtualized list has reused the target row before dispatching an action.
- **Collapsible shared-control panel.** Minimize the in-page panel to the edge of the tab while a task is active.

### Changed

- When visible text is the only change and the previous observation can be reused, shared-control sync can return a text patch. The extension also reuses recent accessibility data and reduces repeated checks during targeted actions.

releases.name: bsk CLI 0.5.0
releases.body:
BrowserSkill CLI 0.5.0 simplifies session management and adds guarded batch actions, reusable recipes, and bounded DOM reads. Use it with extension 0.5.0 for the new observation and interaction features.

### Added

- `bsk open`, `bsk sync`, and `bsk close` manage a browser session for the current caller. Use `--scope <name>` to isolate parallel tasks. Sync returns short context and observation IDs for subsequent actions.
- `bsk plan` runs a sequence of decided actions and stops on the first incomplete step. `bsk recipe` saves and replays verified workflows, with approval for supported reversible steps and a hold when a previous run's outcome is uncertain. Plan is available in MCP and DSH, and recipe tools are opt-in.
- `bsk read` samples bounded DOM fields such as text, attributes, and form state on changing pages. MCP and DSH expose the same read operation. Scripts can declare what they depend on for a narrower pre-action check.
- The daemon records pending browser actions in a local intent ledger. If an action's effect is uncertain, the ledger holds subsequent writes on that tab until reconciliation. Use `bsk sync` to inspect current state and `bsk ledger status` to check the ho

releases.name: BrowserSkill Extension 0.4.2
releases.body:
BrowserSkill Extension 0.4.2 fixes everyday page interaction regressions and improves shared-control reliability, action outcomes, and sensitive-data protection. Pair it with CLI/daemon 0.4.2.

### Added

- **Controller identity:** browser overlays display the agent name, project, session ID, and color supplied by the CLI or DSH client.
- **Date and time inputs:** fill native date, time, datetime-local, month, and week fields, including background-tab handling and format/min/max validation.

### Changed

- Scrolling, ineffective keys, and focusing a text field alone no longer unnecessarily take control from the Agent. Real clicks, keyboard activation, and actual edits still yield to the person. Pending gestures pause dispatch without revoking the current context; coordinate input waits for scrolling to settle.
- Shared control waits for two seconds of quiet after the person's last completed action, up from 650 ms. Completed/cancelled gestures, input-method composition, and native select interactions release their holds correctly.
- Borrowed tabs return relative to their original neighbors, with improved pinned-tab and group restoration. Eligible requests support automatic borrowing

releases.name: bsk CLI 0.4.2
releases.body:
BrowserSkill CLI 0.4.2 adds MCP access and more reliable updates, cancellation, and action outcomes. Use it with extension 0.4.2 for the browser-side fixes below.

### Added

- **MCP server:** `bsk mcp` exposes BrowserSkill over stdio through the existing daemon and extension. `bsk install-skill --mcp` configures Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor. The initial adapter covers its tool schemas; file transfers, recording, and full-page screenshot export remain available through the CLI or DSH plugin.
- **Controller identity:** session startup accepts an agent name, project, and color, shown in the extension's shared-control overlay and session metadata.
- **Date and time inputs:** `fill` supports `date`, `time`, `datetime-local`, `month`, and `week`, with format and min/max validation.

### Changed

- CLI and daemon updates prefer the official website's domestic download source and fall back to GitHub on download or verification failures. Archive fallback stays on the selected version and retains SHA256 verification. Explicit manifest overrides continue to use only the configured source.
- Borrowed tabs return relative to their original neighbors, with improved pinned-tab and group restora

releases.name: BrowserSkill Extension 0.4.1
releases.body:
BrowserSkill 0.4.1 coordinates the CLI/daemon, browser extension and DSH plugin.

### Changed

- **Shared-control default:** new CLI and DSH sync calls select `target` policy.
  DOM actions can reuse the returned control context across completed actions
  and supplementary reads; unrelated page updates no longer require a full-page
  resync. Human intervention or navigation revokes control. Use `--expect` / DSH
  `expect` to protect observed business facts. Scripts, untargeted keys and visual
  actions still require the sync's `--observation` / `observationId` and strict
  observation checks. Select `--policy strict` / `policy: "strict"` on the first
  sync to retain the one-action-per-context workflow; later syncs and steps
  preserve that session's policy.
- CLI/daemon and extension now use protocol 1.8. The new target policy requires
  both peers to support 1.8; update the CLI, running daemon, extension and DSH
  plugin together rather than relying on a successful mixed-version connection.

What you can do

Your goal What BrowserSkill provides
Work where you are already signed in Read documents, search internal sites, and complete web workflows with the browser's existing login state.
Turn instructions into browser actions Read page text and controls, click, type, fill forms, drag items, select ranges, and manage tabs. Capture viewport or full-page screenshots; upload and download files in local mode.

Quick Start

For local automation, you need an AI agent + the bsk CLI + the browser extension. The CLI includes the background daemon. The skill teaches your agent how to use it.

Component Supported environments
CLI / daemon macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel · Linux: x64 and ARM64 · Windows: x64
Extension Chrome and Microsoft Edge, based on Chromium 125 or later. Other Chromium browsers may work; compatibility is not guaranteed.
Agent integration A shell-capable or MCP-capable agent with the BrowserSkill skill (MCP setup).

Let your agent set it up

Send this to your agent:

Set up browser-skill on this machine by following https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/AGENT_INSTALL.md

The guide covers CLI installation, skill setup, connection checks, and a first browser task. You will still need to install the extension in the browser you want to use:

Install for Chrome · Install for Edge

Manual setup

1. Install the CLI

macOS / Linux:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/install.sh | sh
export PATH="${BSK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH"

Windows PowerShell:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/main/install.ps1 | iex

By default, the binary is installed under ~/.local/bin. Check it in the terminal or agent environment that will use it:

bsk --version

If an already-running agent cannot find bsk, restart it to pick up the new PATH, or configure the installed binary's absolute path.

2. Connect the extension

Install it from the Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons, enable the connection and start using it. Local pairing is optional: an unpaired connection stays usable and shows an identity warning. To verify the connection, run bsk daemon pair and paste its link into Connection settings → Pairing link. Pairing is remembered across restarts and upgrades; a paired connection never automatically skips verification after a failure. See local pairing.

3. Install the skill for your agent

bsk install-skill

Select your harness with Space, then press Enter. For non-interactive setup, choose it explicitly:

bsk install-skill --harness cursor --json

Use bsk install-skill --list to see supported targets and paths. Existing installations are skipped unless you explicitly replace them with --force. For another harness, copy the entire crates/bsk-cli/skill/ directory into its skills directory as browser-skill/, including references/.

For MCP clients, bsk install-skill --harness codex --mcp also configures the local stdio server (claude-code and cursor are supported too). See the MCP setup and workflow.

4. Check the connection

bsk doctor

Resolve any failed checks and confirm that the extension shows Connected. Start a new agent session and check that it can discover browser-skill; a successful doctor check alone does not confirm skill discovery.

Try your first task

Once connected, ask your agent:

Use browser-skill to open https://example.com, summarize the page, and end the browser session when finished.

The agent opens its own window in the background, reads the page, returns the summary, and stops its task. External links or manually created tabs that land in the task window are moved to your most recently used normal window; a user window is created if none remain. Routing happens after tab creation, so a tab may briefly appear in the task window. Page-opened tabs and human assistance or recording are preserved. Harnesses that support skill slash commands can also use /browser-skill.

Moving any controlled tab out of its original Agent Window ends the entire browser session, preserves every page in place, and removes its control indicators. Borrowed tabs also stay where they are. Moving a tab back does not resume the task; starting again requires a user decision. Reordering tabs within the same window is unaffected. Normal session stop still returns borrowed tabs and cleans up task pages.

Chrome can still activate a window when a page opens a native popup. For observed task popups, the extension restores the previous Chrome window or minimized state if you have not switched windows. Chrome's public extension APIs cannot guarantee zero transient activation or restore focus to another application.

Try the CLI directly

Start a session and keep the returned session_id:

bsk session start --json

Replace <id> with that value in each command below. With multiple connected browsers, select one using --browser <instance-id-or-name> when starting the session. Background creation is the default; --no-focus remains supported, and --focus explicitly brings the new window forward. Requests for human help and interactive recording still bring the relevant window forward.

bsk navigate https://example.com --session <id>
bsk observe --session <id>
bsk screenshot --session <id> --out example.png
bsk session stop <id>

Use bsk --help or bsk <command> --help for command options. Always stop your session when finished, including after a failed task; borrowed tabs are returned to their original window.

In WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy, or hosts that reap command children, the agent should reuse an existing daemon or run bsk daemon start --foreground in a managed background task, then verify it from a separate tool call. Follow the host setup guide for shared BSK_HOME, BSK_AUTO_START=0, and the independent-terminal fallback when the host cannot keep a task alive.

Close an unused Agent Window

Ask your agent to end its browser session when the task finishes. If a task was interrupted and its Agent Window is still open, list sessions from the same daemon:

bsk session list
bsk session stop SESSION_ID

Use the BROWSER, AGENT WINDOW, and CONTROLLER / PROJECT columns to identify the unused task, then replace SESSION_ID with the value in the SESSION column. When cleanup succeeds, BrowserSkill returns borrowed tabs and closes the task window if no user tabs remain. For a recording you want to save, finish it with bsk record stop.

If the window is absent from the list, confirm you're using the BSK_HOME from that task. If the window is no longer associated with a session, save any work in it and close it in the browser.

DeepSeek Harness plugin

The lightweight DSH plugin (@wxg-prc-cpg/browser-skill-dsh-plugin) packages the canonical browser-skill CLI skill for DeepSeek Harness profiles, automatically adds ~/.local/bin (or a configured bskPath) to the host PATH, and bundles an on-demand bsk CLI + extension setup flow when bsk is not yet installed. Under the hood, it shares the exact same bsk CLI, daemon (DSH_SESSION_ID implicit scoping), and Agent Window runtime as every other agent.

dsh plugin --profile web add @wxg-prc-cpg/browser-skill-dsh-plugin
dsh --profile web

Replace web with your profile name. Invoke /browser-skill in a conversation — if bsk is missing, the agent runs the bundled installer and guides browser extension connection automatically. No separate bsk install-skill step is needed.

Plugin usage and configuration · npm package

Website debugging

Give your agent the browser evidence behind a bug. Start capture before reproducing an issue on a website you are authorized to debug, then inspect the result in the extension or through the agent.

  • Follow an operation: see its requests, console output, form-field values, and immediate or delayed page changes. Capture includes supported manual actions as well as agent actions.
  • Inspect a request: read retained headers, submitted data, response bodies, timing, and errors. Filter traffic or inspect a specific JSON field.
  • Investigate performance: inspect page-load metrics, API timing summaries, and suspected duplicate requests. Missing or partial evidence is identified explicitly.
  • Test and keep evidence: configure task-local request modification, blocking, mock responses, or same-origin replay; save a JSON record to review or share later.

Try a task such as:

Use browser-skill to investigate why saving the form on http://localhost:3000 fails. Start website debugging before reproducing it, inspect the request, response and console, then export the evidence and end the session.

From the extension, open Quick Actions → Website debugging for an existing task. The evidence page connects the operation timeline, requests, Console, page context, Performance, and API analysis. Its history remains accessible after the task ends, even without a daemon connection. A new agent task needs a user-provided export to inspect an ended task's history.

Request replay sends a new request using the page's current session and can change server data. Capture and redaction have limits; retained evidence may still contain sensitive information. See website debugging for the workflow, CLI examples, and limits.

More workflows

Capture a full page

Use Quick Actions → Full-page screenshot for automatic scrolling, a long image you scroll yourself, or the visible area. This extension feature also works without an agent or daemon connection.

For a page in an agent session:

bsk screenshot --session <id> --full-page --out page.png

Agent capture supports background tabs without focusing the window and restores the original scroll position when the document remains available. Full-page capture follows the document's scroll area; nested scrolling panels and virtualized lists have limitations. Screenshot guide

Choose a browser profile

Open the extension in the intended profile and choose Copy profile instructions, then send those instructions with your task. You can also assign a unique Browser name and select it explicitly:

bsk browsers
bsk session start --browser "Work profile" --no-focus --json

The name is set in BrowserSkill; it is not automatically taken from Chrome's profile name. Each session stays bound to the selected instance. Profile selection guide

Add --incognito to isolate a task from the profile's ordinary website login state. Enable the extension's Allow in incognito setting first. Incognito tasks cannot borrow tabs, and all incognito windows in a profile share login state with each other. Incognito guide

Run the agent on a server

Keep the browser and its logins on your computer while the agent, CLI, and daemon run on a server. Pair the extension with that server over authenticated WSS; the browser initiates the connection, so your computer needs no inbound port.

The built-in server supports device pairing, renewal, and revocation. The bsk upload and bsk download file-transfer commands remain local-only. Authorized video exports can write to the CLI machine, including a remote server; Save MP4 as in the extension writes to the browser computer. Remote connection guide

Browser control and privacy

By default, an Agent Window shares the selected profile's login state; it is not a separate account or security sandbox. Agents can act with the permissions of the signed-in websites, so choose the tasks and agent you trust.

New tasks enable shared control automatically. BrowserSkill observes page changes and supported manual activity in controlled tabs so the agent can yield while you edit and synchronize before acting again. This coordination works even when debugging, audit and video recording are off. Use the task's manual hold and resume controls to keep control while you work. Shared-control guide

The extension has two independent Automation settings, both enabled by default:

Setting What it controls
Confirm before borrowing tabs Ask before an agent takes control of one of your existing tabs. Turning it off permits borrowing without that prompt.
Allow requests for human help Let the agent ask you to handle login, verification, or another step that needs your participation.

These browser settings apply to existing and new sessions. Legacy --unattended, tab borrow --no-confirm, and BSK_REQUEST_HELP=off inputs cannot override them. Disabling human help does not mean the requested step was completed. Close the Agent Window to stop its tasks.

BrowserSkill does not operate a mandatory cloud service or collect product telemetry. Automation results go to your selected daemon or gateway and the agent using it; that agent or service may process or retain them under its own policies. The extension does not independently call an AI provider.

Optional history and recordings Where it is saved What to know
Website debugging The current browser profile, including in remote mode Retains captured evidence, including available bodies and field values. Stopped records expire after 30 days, with a 50-record / 50 MiB retention budget and earlier eviction when necessary. Stop capture before deleting a record.
Operation audit The daemon's host, under BSK_HOME/audit Off by default. Records task and operation metadata, excluding input values, page bodies, screenshots, and file contents. Ended tasks expire after 30 days.
Task video The current browser profile; exported copies at the chosen destination Opt-in, silent capture of one authorized tab, limited to 10 minutes / 256 MiB per video. Recordings expire 24 hours after creation; the temporary video budget is 1 GiB. The library supports preview, export and deletion.
Saved observations and step results An explicitly chosen JSON path on the CLI machine, including a remote server --save-full saves the complete reply before display filtering. Files have no automatic expiry; delete them on that machine. view reads historical evidence without refreshing the browser state.

These features offer export and deletion. Stopping a task or disconnecting does not delete retained history or videos; expiration is applied during access or cleanup. Exported copies and copies already received by an agent or gateway must be managed separately. Known secrets are filtered from debugging evidence, but redaction cannot guarantee that all sensitive data is removed. Video frames are not automatically redacted; review visible content before sharing.

Privacy policy · Operation audit · Debugging retention and limits

Updating

For 0.4.1, update the CLI and restart its running daemon before updating the extension. CLI/daemon and extension 0.4.1 use protocol 1.8, which the new default target policy requires on both peers. Updating only the binary leaves a foreground or externally managed daemon on its old version until its host restarts it. Use matching 0.4.1 components for the new workflow.

Existing scripts must follow the shared-control workflow: after initial navigation, synchronize with bsk cooperate sync and pass its context_id as --context. Target-policy DOM actions can reuse that context across actions and supplementary reads; use --expect to protect decision facts. Scripts, untargeted keys and visual actions also require the sync's observation_id as --observation. Synchronize again after human intervention or navigation. Select --policy strict on the first sync to retain one action per context. Reload the updated skill before continuing.

Finish active browser tasks, then update the CLI:

bsk update --yes

Manual and daemon updates fetch the manifest and archives from the official website's domestic download source first, then fall back to GitHub on download, manifest, checksum or archive errors. The GitHub archive fallback is pinned to the selected release and uses the same SHA256 checksum. If both sources fail, the error lists their URLs and individual causes. Setting BSK_UPDATE_MANIFEST_URL explicitly uses only that manifest and its asset URLs, without the built-in public-source fallback.

For the default local setup, this installs the new executable and checks that it runs while the daemon keeps serving, then restarts the daemon from it on the same port. If the restarted daemon does not become ready, the previous executable is put back and the daemon is restarted from it. A daemon started with --foreground is left running on the previous version; restart it in its terminal or supervisor. So is a background daemon when bsk update runs where it could not start one again, such as inside a sandbox whose Windows Job forbids breakaway; restart it with bsk daemon restart outside the sandbox. If you use the installer to replace the binary, restart the daemon afterwards with bsk daemon restart.

A daemon that bsk started in the background also checks for a new release every 30 minutes and, while no agent session is active, installs it the same way. It then starts a daemon from the new executable and exits only once a daemon of the new version serves the same port. If the new daemon exits or is not ready within 20 seconds, it is stopped, and the running daemon puts the previous executable back, serves again on the same port, and retries that release after 6 hours. Browser connections drop for a moment during a handover and reconnect. A daemon that stops for another reason during an update, such as going idle, puts the previous executable back first. A daemon started with --foreground belongs to its terminal or supervisor, so it only reports new releases: run bsk update, then restart the daemon there. If bsk cannot write next to its executable, it only reports new releases; update it with the installer or package manager you used. Set BSK_AUTO_UPDATE=off to disable daemon-side auto-update while keeping manual bsk update available.

bsk doctor shows the last update attempt; update-state.json in the bsk home keeps its stage, result and error. Updates of one executable run one at a time, even from different bsk homes, through .bsk.update.lock (.bsk.exe.update.lock on Windows), which stays next to it. Until an update is confirmed, the previous executable stays next to the new one as .bsk.old-* (.bsk.exe.old-* on Windows); one that is still running remains until its process exits, and a later daemon start removes it. On Windows, self-update renames the running executable, which NTFS supports; where the file system refuses, the update fails and leaves the installation unchanged. bsk supports Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 or later.

Update the extension through its browser store. If you use the DeepSeek Harness plugin, update it in your profile (dsh plugin --profile web update @wxg-prc-cpg/browser-skill-dsh-plugin --latest) and restart that profile. Check bsk --version, bsk status, and bsk doctor. Keep the CLI, running daemon, extension, and optional DSH plugin on matching releases for new features. This README describes the current repository; store builds can lag during review. Check the changelog and releases for availability.

Managed CLI skills update on daemon startup, session start, or doctor while their files remain unchanged. Local edits and custom skills are preserved. Start a new agent session to load updated instructions; doctor reports any paused skill updates.

Custom ports, sandbox hosts, and remote servers

Stop the daemon in its owning host or supervisor, update with bsk update --yes --no-restart-daemon, then start it there with its original flags and BSK_HOME. Use BSK_AUTO_START=0 in agent commands during this process. Follow the sandbox or remote guide for your deployment.

For Developers

The repository is a Rust + pnpm workspace. For a source build, use Rust stable, Node.js 22, and the pnpm version declared in package.json:

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
cargo build --release --locked
pnpm ext:build

The CLI is built under target/release/; load apps/extension/dist/chrome-mv3/ as an unpacked extension. For extension development, use pnpm ext:dev.

Directory Component
crates/bsk-cli CLI, daemon, and bundled agent skill
crates/bsk-protocol Wire types and JSON schemas
apps/extension Browser automation, debugging workspace, and extension UI
packages/dsh-plugin-browserskill Lightweight DeepSeek Harness skill and on-demand setup plugin
packages/ui, packages/i18n, packages/vom Shared UI, localization, and page observation
evals/browser Local test pages and browser capability evaluations

Run cargo test --workspace --locked, pnpm ext:test, and pnpm lint for the relevant checks. See the browser evaluation guide for reproducible browser cases. Bug reports and focused contributions are welcome through GitHub Issues and pull requests; remove sensitive data before attaching browser evidence.

For substantial changes to browser interactions, observations, control policy, or CLI/extension communication, we recommend the optional Agent-driven PR self-check before opening a PR. It tests your current branch through Bsk and records end-to-end evidence. This is not a requirement for opening or merging a PR and does not replace the checks above.

The extension interface supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean, Japanese, French, Italian, Spanish, German, and Brazilian Portuguese. See localization to contribute translations.

Reading dynamic pages (unreleased, protocol 1.9)

Use bsk read for current DOM fields during animation, and extract for tables/ lists. MCP exposes it as bsk_inspect(action=read). A script is checked against the --expect facts it states, or the whole page when it passes --observation; evaluate --unverified is the last resort. Read results never renew action authority: protect business facts with expect. See dynamic reading for query fields, safety boundaries, compatibility and reproducible browser tests.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A tool that connects AI agents to your logged-in browser for automated web tasks.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: BrowserSkill seamlessly links your AI agent to Chrome or Microsoft Edge, allowing it to utilize the accounts you are already signed into. The tool enables agents to read pages, fill out forms, navigate through complex websites, and capture long screenshots. It fundamentally bridges the gap between autonomous AI operations and the authenticated state of a user's daily browser. This allows developers to automate tasks without needing to manage separate login sessions or complex authentication flows for their agents.
keyFeatures: Authenticated session usage: utilizes existing login states from Chrome or Edge.
Page reading: extracts and comprehends content directly from the live browser view.
Form filling: automates data entry tasks across various web forms.
Website navigation: works sequentially through multi-step website interactions.
Screenshot capture: takes extended screengrabs of web pages for documentation or analysis.
